blocks.text: 1. Vanilla RNN

blocks.alt: An RNN cell takes input at t and the previous hidden state to produce output and a new hidden state

blocks.text: Encoder-Decoder Architecture, the final topic of the previous Sequence Models module, formalized a system built from separate, flexible components. Vanilla RNN opens the Recurrent Neural Networks module, the genuinely concrete, simplest network built specifically to process sequences.
It is the genuinely simplest network architecture built specifically to process sequences, a genuinely foundational building block covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Need For A Concrete Network

This connects back to processing one time step at a time, already covered in Time Steps. Every architecture covered throughout the entire Sequence Models module needed some genuinely concrete network to actually do this.

Vanilla RNN is genuinely that concrete network, the simplest one covered in this entire course, giving genuinely concrete substance to the abstract encoder-decoder pattern already covered in the previous module.
3. The Core Idea

blocks.alt: A previous hidden state and current input combine into a new hidden state

blocks.text: Vanilla RNN's genuinely core idea connects back to the hidden state preview, already covered in Time Steps. At each time step, combine the current input with the genuinely previous hidden state.

This directly builds on that earlier preview, turning the genuinely abstract idea of carrying forward a summary into a genuinely concrete, mathematical update rule covered throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 4. The Same Set Of Weights, Every Step

blocks.alt: Step 1 and step 2 both use the same shared weights

blocks.text: This connects back to parameter sharing, already covered in the Convolution Operation. Vanilla RNN genuinely reuses the exact same set of weights at every single time step, no matter how long the sequence is.

This is a genuinely direct parallel to parameter sharing, just applied across time instead of across spatial position, keeping the network's own parameter count genuinely independent of sequence length.
5. The Recurrent Connection

blocks.alt: The hidden state at t feeds forward to the hidden state at t+1

blocks.text: A genuinely defining structural feature has the genuinely previous hidden state feed back into the network as part of its own current input, a genuinely distinctive loop-like structure.
This is called a recurrent connection, giving this entire architecture family its own distinctive name, the exact feature that lets information genuinely persist across time steps.
6. Output At Every Step

blocks.alt: An output is produced at every time step t=1, t=2, t=3

blocks.text: This connects back to Sequence-to-Sequence Learning, already covered in the previous module. A Vanilla RNN can genuinely produce an output at every single time step, not just at the very end.
This is a genuinely flexible design that supports many genuinely different sequence task shapes, from one output per input step to just one final output, depending on how the network gets used.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This flexibility, already covered in this topic, is exactly why Vanilla RNNs and their more advanced successors, covered later in this module, could be adapted to genuinely so many different sequence tasks throughout this course.

blocks.text: 7. The Role Of The Activation Function
This connects back to Tanh, already covered in the Activation Functions module. The hidden state update genuinely applies an activation function, commonly Tanh, at every single time step.

This directly reuses the activation function concept already covered throughout that earlier module, keeping the hidden state values genuinely bounded and well behaved across potentially many repeated updates.
8. A Preview Of An Important Limitation

blocks.alt: Vanilla RNN struggles with long-range dependencies

blocks.text: A genuinely important, honest limitation connects back to Vanishing Gradients, already covered generally in Activation Functions. Vanilla RNN genuinely struggles to remember information from far earlier time steps.
This genuinely real limitation, already covered in this section, is explored in complete depth in the very next two topics of this module, both dedicated specifically to this exact problem.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Vanilla RNN Is Genuinely Still Worth Understanding

blocks.alt: A short sequence task points toward considering vanilla RNN

blocks.text: This connects back to the hidden state and recurrent connection, both already covered in this topic. Every more advanced architecture covered later in this module genuinely builds directly on these exact core ideas.
Genuinely short sequences where its own limitation, already covered, matters less are another genuine case where Vanilla RNN, already covered, can genuinely remain a reasonable, simple choice.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates a genuinely simple Vanilla RNN update rule, processing a sequence one time step at a time, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
hidden_size = 4
input_size = 3

W_input = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, input_size)) * 0.1   # already covered as the same set of weights, every step
W_hidden = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1  # already covered as the recurrent connection

def rnn_step(x_t, h_previous, W_input, W_hidden):
    # already covered as the core idea in this topic: combine current input with previous hidden state
    return np.tanh(W_input @ x_t + W_hidden @ h_previous)  # already covered as the role of the activation function

sequence = [rng.normal(size=input_size) for _ in range(5)]  # already covered as Time Steps in the previous module
hidden_state = np.zeros(hidden_size)

for t, x_t in enumerate(sequence):
    hidden_state = rnn_step(x_t, hidden_state, W_input, W_hidden)
    print(f"Time step {t}: hidden state = {np.round(hidden_state, 3)}")

print("\nNotice: the exact same W_input and W_hidden weights, already covered in this topic, were reused at every single time step")

blocks.content: Running this example shows the hidden state evolving across time steps, with the exact same weights reused throughout, exactly the core update rule and parameter sharing already covered as this topic's own foundational mechanism.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Vanilla RNN is the simplest network architecture built specifically to process sequences.
At each time step, it combines the current input with the previous hidden state.
It reuses the exact same set of weights at every time step, keeping parameter count independent of length.
The recurrent connection feeds the previous hidden state back in as part of the current step's input.
It can produce an output at every time step, supporting many different sequence task shapes.
The hidden state update applies an activation function, commonly Tanh, at every step.
It genuinely struggles to remember information from far earlier time steps.
Every more advanced architecture covered later in this module builds directly on these core ideas.
